## Daily routine (automated)

Times are UTC+07:00 (local time), as of notes from 19 Oct 2026 onward.

- 03:00: hermes-settings-backup, no-agent mode, no LLM tokens; sends a short statistics report to Telegram.
- 03:05: hindsight-memory-backup.
- 09:00: Computer Vision lesson (daily-learning-computer-vision) to Telegram topic 35. One new concept per day, never repeated. Last covered digital image representation (17 Oct); convolution is next.
- 09:05: Arabic Dars Yaum lesson (daily-learning-arabic) to topic 35. Each day has 3 fi'il verbs (madhi, mudhari', amr, masdar), 3 mufrodat, 1 Saudi 'ammiyah expression, and a speaking challenge. No repeated material; 16–17 Oct covered dhamir munfashil, then al-Idhafah.
- 21:20: dotfiles-backup. Runs chezmoi re-add, commits, pushes to GitHub, and notifies Telegram.

## Weekly and periodic

- Every 7 days: Arabic grammar review (nahwu and sharf), tied to the daily lessons.
- Periodic, time not recorded: brain-vault compile (job brain-vault-compile) for the Obsidian vault. Runs ingest, link, lint, then commit and push; reports to Telegram.
- Mengaji study group (Makkah & Madinah Mengaji, ustadz Abdul Wahhab, Lc., M.A.): planned for Wednesdays after Maghrib, every two weeks, about 20:00–21:00. About 5–7 members, meeting at Masjid As Sakinah Nusantara (Nustro). Next session recorded as Wed 21 Oct 2026, but exact dates are unconfirmed; verify today's session.

## Work and schedule constraints

- Works remotely from Indonesia as a Data Engineer at Hassad Food, Qatar.
- Operational data is usually delivered daily on a T-1 basis (previous day's transactions).
- Agrico data was once weekly on Thursdays; this older record may no longer apply.
- Master's program: three semesters, two periods each. No formal thesis deadline recorded; in Feb 2026 the user estimated about six months of working time remained.
- Qatar work status (visa, contract, on-site policy) unresolved as of Oct 2026. A 2025 note warned the contract could end in December if the visa issue was unsolved; no newer deadline is recorded.

## Schedule conflict to confirm

- 17 Oct 2026, 04:33: user asked for all jobs at 21:00, 21:05, and 21:15 with 5-minute gaps.
- 17 Oct 2026, 13:56: later record sets lessons at 09:00 and 09:05. These are treated as current as the latest.
- Not recorded whether lesson jobs moved back to 21:00. The user should confirm.
- Both lessons failed to deliver on 17 Oct because python-telegram-bot was missing. The assistant installed it, but a clean scheduled run is unconfirmed. The user should check the two topic 35 messages directly.

## How the user wants to be checked in on and reminded

- Telegram is the primary channel, in the "Digmi Laboratorium" group. Lessons go to topic 35. Every scheduled job reports there, with each job's chat kept separate.
- Failures must always surface. After an earlier laptop failure and data loss, reliable backup reporting is a top priority.
- Style: practical, direct, specific. Give step-by-step guidance and explain the cause of errors, not just a workaround. For errors, send the full traceback, not only the last line.
- Candor over polish: admit uncertainty rather than invent answers, and use concrete real-scenario examples.
- Lessons are bite-sized, one concept per day, built progressively without repetition.
- Pending check-ins: verify a clean scheduled Telegram run; decide whether to move lesson jobs back to 21:00; copy the Hermes GPG backup passphrase from the macOS Keychain into a password manager (open since 17 Oct). The MacBook pickup from a friend returning to Indonesia was planned for about 8 Nov 2026, but the repair is recorded as complete, so the pickup may not be needed. Confirm with the friend before 8 Nov.

## Who the user is

The user is Imam Taufiq (also used the name Imam Digmi for some online accounts). He holds an S.Kom. and is pursuing an MTI (Magister Teknologi Informasi) at BINUS University, started September 2025, and is in the thesis stage. He lives in the Bogor area of Indonesia, works remotely, and his main languages are Indonesian (primary) and English for technical and professional work. He is also learning Arabic (Fusha, with interest in Saudi 'Ammiyah).

He aims to continue to a PhD, with KAUST as his first choice and interest in Saudi Arabia more broadly. Target fields are Data Science, Data Engineering, Computer Vision, AI and remote sensing. He wants a research portfolio strong enough for PhD applications and wants to publish in Q1 or Q2 journals. Thesis supervisor target: Prof. Dr. Sani Muhamad Isa, S.Si., M.Kom.

## Important people in his life

- Wife (pasangan): married; they travelled together to Singapore (Bugis) in October 2026. Name not recorded.
- Child: about 13–14 months old as of September–October 2026. He plans family trips around the child's comfort and extra time needs. In September 2026 the whole family had flu and the child tested positive for Influenza A.
- Mother (ibu): travelled to Makkah and was scheduled to return in September 2026 (recorded as historical).
- Ustadz Abdul Wahhab, Lc., M.A.: teacher for the Makkah & Madinah Mengaji study circle at Masjid As Sakinah Nusantara (Nustro).
- A friend: returning to Indonesia around 8 November 2026 and may bring back his repaired MacBook Pro.
- Colleagues and contacts from work or visa matters, recorded without detail: Essam (Dandy data support), Reza (visa), Samer (VM and Ministry database work).

## Preferences: how he likes answers

- Practical, direct and specific communication (Indonesian: 'praktis, langsung, dan spesifik').
- Length should match the question: very short answers for simple factual questions, quick translations and quizzes; longer, deep explanations for complex technical topics, which he is willing to read.
- Accuracy matters most. He prefers the assistant to admit uncertainty rather than invent information, and he will correct wrong answers. He wants evidence, documentation or references behind answers, and prefers academic references in APA 7th edition.
- He compares options before deciding and wants trade-offs (performance, cost, complexity, technical and financial factors weighed together). He favours pragmatic solutions that fit real resource limits and will accept a simpler tool over enterprise technology when the problem does not need it.
- He likes concrete examples based on real scenarios, ready-to-run terminal commands, Python code or SQL queries, and ASCII or Mermaid diagrams for technical pipelines.
- He prefers technical terms kept in English (pipeline, deployment, ingestion, orchestration) even when writing in Indonesian.
- For Arabic: he prefers Fusha unless he asks for Amiyyah, likes harakat by default, wants natural idiomatic Saudi expressions rather than literal translations, and wants corrections when an Arabic phrase is off. For practice with many sentences he likes a table with Arabic text beside the Indonesian translation. For quick translation mode, 'in:' means Indonesian to Arabic and 'ar:' means Arabic to Indonesian.
- Code reviews: minimal code, no speculative abstractions, concrete bugs with path:line references, hard defects separated from optional smells, under 400 words.
- Debugging: when errors occur (for example with vLLM), send the full traceback, not only the last line.
- He does not want installed library code modified; he prefers workarounds such as a project-level sitecustomize.py or flags.
- Database safety: SELECT-only access. Any INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP or other mutation must be shown as a SQL block for him to run himself, and he approves each query first.
- He does not want previously taught Arabic words or CV concepts repeated in daily lessons.
- He wants decision support that weighs technical and financial factors, and he values a critical check on agent-generated research.
- Manual sync: he updates dotfiles on other devices with `chezmoi update`, not by cron, to avoid overwriting unpushed local changes.

## Platforms and tools he uses

- Telegram is his main channel for agent notifications and scheduled job reports. Output goes to the 'Digmi Laboratorium' group, topic 35, with separate messages per topic. He wants all scheduled job reports sent there.
- Hermes Agent on macOS (desktop and CLI) is his personal AI assistant. He manages work through kanban tasks and delegates project file changes to it. He uses Hindsight as its external memory provider.
- He has explored WhatsApp integration with Hermes, asking whether it needs a new phone number or SIM. No outcome is recorded.
- Work stack: macOS with Homebrew and zsh, Apple Silicon (vLLM and vllm-metal, MLX), Python (3.14 for the automap project, managed with uv), SQL and Azure SQL, Azure Data Factory, Azure Blob Storage, PowerShell for automation, a Windows VM accessed through Windows App for GIS work, GitHub, Obsidian (brain vault), and CVAT for image annotation.
- Dotfiles are managed with chezmoi in the GitHub repo imamdigmi/dotfiles, across Linux, macOS and Windows.

## Daily routine and recurring commitments

- 09:00 every day: Computer Vision lesson (one new small concept per day) delivered to Telegram topic 35.
- 09:05 every day: Arabic lesson (3 fi'il verbs, 3 vocabulary words, one Saudi 'Ammiyah expression and a speaking challenge), delivered to Telegram topic 35. The lessons need the Hermes gateway running before 09:00.
- Backup jobs: hermes-settings-backup at 03:00 and hindsight-memory-backup at 03:05, which alert only on failure, and dotfiles-backup at 21:20. On 17 October 2026 he asked for the backups to move to 21:00, 21:05 and 21:15, but later records still show the old times. Treat the backup times as unconfirmed.
- Mengaji study circle: planned every other Wednesday, about 20:00–21:00 after Maghrib, at Masjid As Sakinah Nusantara, with 5–7 participants. Status is planned, not confirmed.
- Home workout: barbell, two 10 kg plates, two 3 kg dumbbells, resistance bands, a bench and a kettlebell.

## Open items to surface (as of 21 October 2026)

- Wednesday 21 October 2026 (today): the mosque permit letter (surat permohonan izin kegiatan) is due. It must say there will be no speakers or loudspeakers (tanpa speaker / pengeras suara) and include a photo. Submission is not confirmed. The 19 October Telegram reminder was not delivered, so it should be sent again and delivery confirmed.
- Work follow-up from 19 October: review review_calibration.csv (100 candidate product pairs) and report back. No date is recorded. Later guidance was to stop the bulk review and open the HTML report instead, so confirm which step is still needed.
- MacBook Pro: the repair is confirmed complete and the machine works normally. The friend's return around 8 November 2026 may no longer be needed; he has not said.
- MTI thesis: no deadline recorded. A February 2026 estimate of about six months implies around August 2026, but this is an unconfirmed inference.
- Telegram delivery: on 17 October the reports failed because python-telegram-bot was missing. It has since been installed, but he should check the two lesson messages visually because API status alone does not prove delivery.
- GPG key: his signed commits show only as 'Verified' locally until the public key is added at github.com/settings/gpg/new.

The routines snapshot is marked stale, so the schedule above is the most recent recorded state rather than a confirmed one.
